title: On Restricting the sale to villagers only
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：restrict　|　正文 356 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 restrict 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1976 the musician ① restricted the sale to villagers only without a word of thanks, and every listener in the hall said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the musician ② restricts the sale to villagers only at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ restrict the sale to villagers only at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ restricted the sale to villagers only before — a line in the programme for December 1970 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Restricting the sale to villagers only without a word of thanks, the musician said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the score at the far piano, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ restrict the talk to one single point at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Restrict the talk to one single point at once and never mention it again.

By 1983 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the programme, and a new listener from the next hall ⑧ restricts the talk to one single point without a word of thanks every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the piano, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ restricted the sale to villagers only again when nobody else would.

⑩ To restrict the sale to villagers only, my mother said in 1988, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the hall remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the hall forgets, somebody restricts the sale to villagers only at once again and somebody must restrict the sale to villagers only without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 限制（一般过去式 restricted the sale to villagers only：1976 年乐师头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 限制（一般现在 restricts the sale to villagers only：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 限制（不定式 to restrict the sale to villagers only：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 限制（过去完成时 had restricted the sale to villagers only：1970 年十二月的节目单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 限制（动名词 restricting the sale to villagers only 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 限制在（restrict the talk to one single point：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去限制在把话头限定在一点之上）
G. v. 限制在（restrict the talk to one single point：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 限制（后段两处：新来的听客照例 restricts the talk to one single point，而母亲又一次 restricted the sale to villagers only）

answers.why: restrict 意为“限制”，1976 年乐师不图一句谢限制把买卖只限在本村人之间，那是音乐厅里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 restricted。
restrict 意为“限制”，自那以后乐师二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 restricts。
restrict 意为“限制”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯限制把买卖只限在本村人之间”，此处为不定式 to restrict the sale to villagers only。
restrict 意为“限制”，节目单里 十二月 那行字说明早在 1983 年之前就有人限制过，故用过去完成时 had restricted。
restrict 意为“限制”，乐师说“限制把买卖只限在本村人之间这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 restricting the sale to villagers only 作主语。
restrict 意为“限制在”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去限制在把话头限定在一点之上”，should ever 之后用原形 restrict the talk to one single point。
restrict 意为“限制在”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻限制在把话头限定在一点之上（restrict the talk to one single point at once），以后再也不要提起。
restrict 意为“限制”，新来的听客每个夜晚都照例限制在把话头限定在一点之上，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 restricts。
restrict 意为“限制”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢限制把买卖只限在本村人之间，用一般过去式 restricted 叙述。
restrict 意为“限制”，结尾那句是母亲 1988 年的话：要限制把买卖只限在本村人之间，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和音乐厅记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 restrict 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1976 the musician restricted the sale to villagers only without a word of thanks, and nobody in the hall forgot it.
Even now the musician restricts the sale to villagers only at once whenever the hall asks.
Restricting the sale to villagers only without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever restrict the talk to one single point at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new listener from the next hall restricts the talk to one single point without a word of thanks every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother restricted the sale to villagers only again, and the hall remembered that half.
